family_assessments.assessment: Retain the cut-off test. The intended challenge is to decide whether an already signed trustee handover took effect before the bank meeting, not to choose the latest or most formal-looking record. The blind review (family_a/review/blind-review.md) found that registered release effects simultaneous retirement and replacement, while an affirmative hold preserves the incumbent; the hold is not a missing release entry. Fresh excerpt readings verified the joint instrument-and-disposition routes and rejected a proposed shorter route (family_a/review/necessity.md). A0/A1 preserve the key and context under a Source reorder; A0/A2 vary only the disposition (family_a/review/matched-sources.json and the register). The bank and administrative material add a supported kinship and non-operative details. A later note and frequency favour the incumbent; promotion of signed draft wording favours the successor. The explanatory terms and single two-person office limit generalisation.
family_assessments.overlap: The joint proof overlaps B and C. D holds effectiveness fixed and varies scope; A does not test execution status among counterparts, the distinction between title progress and office, or an absent original.

family_assessments.assessment: Retain the attribution contrast. B0/B1 vary one name field for the same dated conversation. The independently maintained attendance field binds the native parentage statement to one named speaker only in the completed condition (family_b/review/outputs/comparison.json). In the incomplete condition both speakers remain compatible and the readers preserve the independently supported ordinary parent edge (family_b/review/agreement.json). The forward and export share one informant; forward-only readings do not settle the speaker (family_b/review/mask-results.json). Deleting a needed identity or statement fact defeats the target without removing unaffected kinship (family_b/review/proof-deletions.json). The clerk's original-document sighting provides ordinary kinship through a distinct information path. The benchmark can be shortcut at graph level by checking field completeness and choosing the first contact; do not equate the exact graph with successful attribution proof.
family_assessments.overlap: B and C both withhold under incomplete identifiers, but B identifies the speaker, not a trust endpoint. F keeps the distinguishing identity evidence complete. B establishes common origin for one relay lineage, not a causal repetition effect or independent conflict.

family_assessments.assessment: Retain the distributed trust-endpoint test. C0/C1 switch only the linked parent-deed reference; C2 obscures its distinguishing character. The comparison shows the supported trust endpoint switching, and both readers withhold both focal allocations when the reference is partial (family_c/review/outputs/comparison.json; family_c/review/agreement.json). Fresh excerpt readers verified the three-Source proof; whole-file masks defeat the target while preserving ten ordinary edges (family_c/review/proof-deletions.json). Shared trustees, a wish, an expense and routine meeting details create context. First-trust, fixed-trust and assign-both rules fail across the variants, but the choice is bounded to two parallel settlements and one decisive register entry. The invariant graph checks completeness in this file, not the effect of context load.
family_assessments.overlap: Shares joint proof with A and incomplete-information restraint with B. It allocates one designation between trusts; it does not show whether real movement of assets propagates relationships between already identified trusts.

family_assessments.assessment: Retain the admitted scoped amendment; refine future deletion checks rather than altering the admitted case. The approved premise was that changing one operative provision locator would switch which earlier beneficiary survives while preserving the trust, replacement and unaffected relationships. The register's D0/D1 matched-control observation records that exact result and that the saved keys attach joint scope proof to each current beneficiary; grouped proof was independently verified in the closing audit. Separate office and beneficiary provisions and the variation's own effective date supply context without changing the comparison. Individual fact-level deletions remain incomplete, and following the locator alone can reproduce the graph without the full proof. The invariants are trust relationships, not a test of unrelated kinship completeness.
family_assessments.overlap: A asks whether an act took effect; D assumes effectiveness and asks what the act displaced. It does not establish implied repeal, multigeneration carry-forward or a branch-dependent proof for an invariant earlier beneficiary.

family_assessments.assessment: Retain the bounded label-collision test. The approved premise was that changing one populated display label would leave the exact graph and sufficient proof routes unchanged when stable references and complete identity links were fixed. The register's F0/F1 comparison records invariant graphs and separately attached proofs, and its masked review records that withholding an exact identity entry defeats its dependent edge. The original isolated excerpt reader identified the right person in the explanation but entered a different structured surname; the independent identical-packet repeat returned the correct surname. Preserve both observations. The working index is ancillary, the exact identity reconciliation is authoritative in the file, and positional pairing remains a shortcut. This is not a collision in authoritative identifiers.
family_assessments.overlap: Unlike B, neither branch removes distinguishing identity information. F checks exact names and correct-person attachment, but not a former-name bridge with incomplete reconciliation or ambiguity across multiple authoritative records.

gaps.finding: B and C withhold when a missing discriminator would change the named edge; L limits proof to the field actually available, and R is an attempt concerning an exact event date. None checks whether every date consistent with a bounded observation gives the same result, versus a range that straddles the operative boundary.

The portfolio verifies several joins, but not the cumulative exhaustion of a named provision through distinct qualifying financial completions. O keeps administrative progress separate from office; the pending asset-transfer case keeps movement separate from beneficiary designation. Neither requires reconciling failed or duplicated posting appearances into an operative total.

Conflict is no longer an empty area at technical qualification: E and W cover independent disagreement, while B verifies a single origin and its relay. These do not verify a causal repetition effect or a general priority rule. D covers one express amendment and N adds technical coverage of execution status; other amendment mechanisms and exhaustive individual fact-level necessity checks remain open.

C verifies invariant completeness under a target intervention. X supplies a technically qualified assertion-versus-logistics control, not a burial, placement or volume control. T supplies a technically qualified intermediate full-file inspection case, not a causal workload comparison or authority to count an unchecked item as verified. Broader interaction claims need interpretable component controls; proof masks alone do not provide them. The registered large-tier commitment remains separate.

Retrieval, requesting unseen papers, OCR and recovery of physical text would change the scope. A stipulated limit in a readable, supplied record can be scored only for its consequences for supported Person/Trust relationships.

result.portfolio_summary:
Count one independent Matter history per family, not per matched condition or diagnostic mask. Five families are formally admitted: A, B, C, D and F. Seven more are technically qualified but are not counted as admissions: X (firsthand support in native routine correspondence), T (the scope of a completed inspection in an intermediate supplied file), N revision 3 (execution status among retained counterparts), E revision 3 (independent parentage agreement versus disagreement), W revision 2 (independent accounts of current trustee office), O revision 7 (matched title-application progress with office and its proof fixed), and L revision 9 (the evidentiary limit of the civil-record version actually sighted, with identities fixed). E0 and E1 remain diagnostic only; the earlier realism return is not an admission of E revision 3. E and W already give conflict coverage, with different designs; W's account removals are proof diagnostics, not matched benchmark conditions. The packet supplies no paid extraction observations or sealed evaluation inputs. Technical qualification is evidence about the file and its key, not about extractor performance.

The admitted histories repeatedly exercise exact named endpoints, cross-Source joins, documentary authority and same-edge sufficiency. They isolate different mechanisms: A tests operative effect and presentation order, D tests amendment scope after effectiveness is fixed, B and C test different reasons to withhold a named edge, and F tests invariance under an ancillary label collision with complete evidence. C's ten invariant edges test completeness; its routine material does not establish a distraction or volume effect. Treat H, I, J, M, P, Q, R, S and U as retained attempts, not additional verified coverage. Keep the registered intermediate and large workload commitments separate. Source count and length describe a file; neither measures reasoning difficulty or the effort of acquiring the file.

Reserve rank: BN first, for a comparatively economical test of when bounded evidence suffices even without an exact underlying date; BO second, for a natural closing file in which a cumulative operative amount must be reconstructed without mistaking bookkeeping for completed payment. BO costs more and should advance only if an ordinary complete reconciliation leaves the intended distinction observable. These two reserves are not commissions and do not fill the seven-history gap from twelve technically qualifying histories to the pre-giant goal of nineteen. Do not fill that gap by counting variants or approving weaker duplicates.

evidence_dependencies: Fresh readers reconstruct the earliest and latest dates consistent with each checked age. Verify exact excerpts for the age and its observation date, the provision-to-person and provision-to-trust links, the rule and the cut-off. A table citation must include the row's exact person and its governing heading or local reference, not an age cell beside somebody else's name.

Test the signed designation, readiness check and plausible shorter subsets for sufficiency. Separately delete the checked age, its as-of date and the scope link or threshold fact. Remove any copies of each deleted fact and rederive both complete keys. Look specifically for an earlier dated age check, a birth date in the designation, or a copied or independently certified threshold finding in the briefing that might preserve the edge.

Distinguish a confirmed interval spanning the boundary from a missing or unreliable observation, and verify the unrelated relationship separately. Credit any genuinely sufficient subset; do not mandate the investment statement or a redundant cut-off citation.
design.expected_sensitivity_or_invariance: Only support for the focal beneficiary edge changes. The strongest positive proof combines the named row, the express commencement rule, the checked age and its as-of date, and the review cut-off where needed. In the straddling branch the exact bounds admit both a threshold already passed and one still to come. Record that uncertainty without a negative predicate or inferred alternative designee.
genres_and_provenance: Verified governing extract from the trustees' executed file: identifies the trust, the express commencement rule and an unrelated continuing relationship.
Signed designation retained in the decision file: supplies the exact named person and the local provision reference, without claiming that the person has reached the threshold.

Dated trustee readiness check retained with the administration papers: identifies the person and relevant provision and records completed years at an expressly identified observation date, based on a direct identity-record check. It does not certify a current roster.
Dated investment provider statement retained with the cash-planning papers: shows the balance available for the upcoming cycle from the provider's own books, not the capacity of any named recipient.
Dated adviser briefing note retained on the advice file: records the planning question and fixes the cut-off without deciding it.
design.intervention: Replace exactly one literal completed-years value in the readiness check. Keep the as-of date, identity, knowledge basis, issue and receipt dates, all other bytes and Source order fixed.
invariants: Trust, named designation, prescribed age, reporting precision, cut-off, available funds and independent ordinary relationships remain fixed.
The comparison does not change who was checked, the instrument's effect rule, or the authority of the checker.
negative_controls: Earmarked funds and references to a forthcoming payment do not establish commencement in either branch. Masking the provider statement preserves both graph keys.
The unrelated continuing relationship keeps its independent proof in both branches and target-only diagnostics.
design.scenario: The adviser must join a named designation to the instrument's age rule and a checked but imprecise age observation. The records are sufficient without further enquiry only when every date consistent with the observation places commencement before the briefing.
shortcut_heuristics: Test age-token, exact-date-required, issue-date-as-observation, reserved-funds-as-benefit and nearest-person rules. A value comparison can predict the delta without establishing the same-edge proof.
Audit headings, filenames, copied notes, row grouping and position for leakage; use reordered presentation only in review.
success_criteria: Two isolated full-file readers per branch reconstruct the complete exact-name graph and distinguish supported commencement from a straddling interval. Fresh readers reproduce the bounds, exact positive subset, reason for withholding and separately rederived mask keys.

Stop if the natural check would give a precise birth date or its own current-status verdict, if an ordinary controlling record must be excluded, if the age value changes another fact in the fixed file, or if the two branches cannot be distinguished without an unstated rule.

feasibility.authoring_and_review_effort: Estimated person-hours: authoring and boundary checks 8–12; isolated whole-file and fresh excerpt or removal review 9–14; adjudication and audit 6–9; owner review 2–4. Assumes four complete reads and at most one pre-lock revision.
feasibility.documentary_complexity: Nominal 5 natural Sources. The governing extract, signed designation, readiness check, provider balance statement and briefing serve separate rule, decision, verification, cash-planning and review purposes. Five is a planning inventory, not a typical file size.
feasibility.infrastructure_reuse: Reuse A's cut-off audit, C's independently rederived diagnostic keys and existing exact-byte and same-edge sufficient-subset checks.
feasibility.ontology_compatibility: Use beneficiary_of and independently supported invariant predicates with exact Person and Trust endpoints. Age, thresholds, pending proof and the payment plan belong in evidence or the companion register.
risks_and_limits: The checked value may be an easy lexical predictor; graph agreement alone does not establish bounded inference.
This tests one stipulated commencement rule. It does not establish how age is normally verified or how real instruments treat age-dependent payments.

assumptions: The supplied terms make the threshold a condition of the named provision itself, not merely of payment to an already established beneficiary. The terms or supplied check explicitly define how to read completed years and the boundary; no outside law or convention is needed.

A trustee's dated result in completed years serves an actual forward-planning task and is reliable for that stated precision. The advice file would ordinarily receive that result without the underlying identity document or a separate exact date already available for this review.
Both checked ages are credible in the same documentary situation. The dates are chosen away from leap-day and boundary-equality complications, and fixed material does not presuppose either result.
grounding.documentary_situation: The instrument makes commencement of a named provision automatic at a specified age. For the readiness review, a trustee supplies a dated check recording the named person's age in completed years as at a fixed date, from identity evidence the trustee checked directly. The retained result does not reproduce the date of birth. A provider statement accounts for funds earmarked for the next cycle, independently of any determination that the provision has commenced.
grounding.legal_workflow: Review the named provisions and funds set aside for an upcoming trust payment cycle.
grounding.meeting_purpose: Distinguish a current named beneficiary relationship from a designation whose commencement remains unverified at the briefing date.
practitioner_unknowns: Would the trustee naturally retain and share a completed-years check for this meeting without sending a precise birth date or a conclusive commencement statement?
Would the provider's funds statement and the operative records normally be available at this readiness review without a later payment instruction that already settles the relationship?

references.relevance: Supports keeping operative decisions and investment and payment records. It does not establish an age-check format, an age threshold or the effect of reaching it.
references.title: HMRC · Records to keep for trusts

grounding.retainer: Advise whether an individually designated benefit has begun under the trust's express age rule, separately from preparing funds for payment.

objective.coverage_gap: R compares an exact event date with an operative deadline; it cannot test a correct decision that is invariant across several possible underlying dates. L removes access to a parentage entry rather than preserving a genuine bounded observation. AG varies the coverage of receipt logs; here the checked observation is substantive in both branches and the uncertainty concerns the individual's possible threshold date.
objective.failure_mechanism: An extractor may insist on an exact birth date, use the earlier checked age as the current age, round an indeterminate range into a verdict, or treat earmarked funds as evidence of current status.
objective.falsifiable_hypothesis: Changing only the verified completed-years value changes support for the named edge when it moves the possible threshold dates from wholly before the review to straddling it. The first branch supports the edge; the second leaves it unresolved without disproving it. Exact recovery and sufficient attachment in both branches disconfirm the predicted errors.

proposals.title: An age check can establish commencement without an exact birth date

evidence_dependencies: Fresh readers first reconstruct the transaction history and the operative provision separately, then verify exact subsets joining the named row, rule, full-period coverage, qualifying amounts and relevant outcomes. When entries for other people or payment purposes are adjacent, quote the relevant row with its person or provision heading and amount and reference, then quote the outcome with that same transaction identifier and the provider's status meaning. A bare amount, status or page citation does not carry the join.

Check the strongest shorter route through the signed schedule, operative extract and verified reconciliation. If the reconciliation independently establishes a complete qualifying amount for that provision, credit it without demanding redundant bank citations. Otherwise test the primary instruction and provider routes and accept either verified sufficient subset.

Before claiming necessity, search for the same failure in a return line, an exception report and a derived reconciliation note; for amounts in both postings and instructions; and for the same scope or coverage in carried balances or totals. Separate deletion of a fact from masking one appearance. Have independent readers rederive all diagnostic graphs, including any route that survives.
design.expected_sensitivity_or_invariance: The intact graph supports the continuing capped benefit. The settled installments provide positive evidence of the applicable total; the linked provider failure gives affirmative evidence for excluding an apparently relevant debit. If deletion leaves resolution of a potentially cap-reaching installment or a relevant period open, withhold unless another sufficient route survives. Do not turn the weakened file into a finding that the cap was reached.
genres_and_provenance: Verified governing extract retained in the trustees' operative papers: identifies the trust, the cap and cessation rule, the permitted payment path and an unaffected continuing relationship.
Signed named schedule retained in the decision file: identifies the person and the operative provision by its ordinary reference without giving a running completion total.

Trustee-authorised installment instruction record retained in the payment workstream: links the authorised attempts to the provision and records any planned reissue as an instruction, not a completion.
Provider account statement retained for accounts: supplies the dated postings and their transaction references from the provider's books, including the cash debit and return.

Provider's native settlement and exception report retained by the payment operator and supplied for reconciliation: gives the actual outcomes from its own transaction records and links the failed transfer to the corresponding posting.

Trust accountant's period reconciliation retained with the accounts: resolves the postings against the instructions, documents coverage and any separately charged costs, and discloses when it derives a fact from a provider record.
Dated adviser brief retained on the advice file: sets the review boundary and separates the current-provision question from reconciling cash.
design.intervention: Score one intact natural condition. In review only, separately remove the cap or qualifying rule, the exact provision-to-transaction link, the noncompletion fact, and a necessary payment amount or coverage bound, including copies and derived restatements as appropriate. Mask the reconciliation separately to test what the original records can still establish. Do not edit a posted amount or a return status as a scored sibling: the related records would no longer describe a coherent transaction.
invariants: The intact file has one exact trust and person roster, one cut-off, one set of transaction outcomes and one full accounting period for the focal provision.
The unrelated trust relationship retains independent proof in focal diagnostics. Provider or accounting entries do not change their documentary meaning when another Source is removed.
negative_controls: A planned reissue and separately charged costs do not count as completed installments. Repeated appearances of a transaction in the account statement and reconciliation do not count as additional installments.
The unrelated trust relationship survives deletion of the focal facts and masking of the payment records.
design.scenario: A single ordinary reconciliation file supports both a genuine cash-accounting task and a separate current-provision question. The same payment attempt appears in more than one record, and a returned debit has an affirmative noncompletion trail. Settled amounts—not the number of entries, gross outflow or whether funds are available—determine whether the provision continues.
shortcut_heuristics: Test gross-debit totals, payment-means-beneficiary, latest-balance, duplicate counting and failure-by-absence. Check whether a nearby expense row or superficially similar transaction code could be attached to the right edge but the wrong payment.
Audit headings, filenames, Source position and copied accountant summaries. Return the design if an ordinary self-contained roster bypasses the cap reconstruction; do not hide it.
success_criteria: Two isolated complete-file readers independently recover every exact-name edge and reconcile the qualifying total. Fresh readers agree on the strongest positive route, the exact exclusion of the failed debit, sufficient alternative subsets if any and independently rederived removal results.

Stop if the payment trail cannot establish completeness or noncompletion, if the arithmetic depends on an unstated financial rule, if the capped provision is not natural, or if preserving the scientific distinction would require omitting an ordinarily retained controlling record.

feasibility.authoring_and_review_effort: Estimated person-hours: authoring and reconciliation integration 11–16; blind whole-file and fresh excerpt or removal review 10–15; adjudication and audit 7–11; owner review 3–5. Assumes two whole-file reads, a separate reconciliation pass and at most one pre-lock revision.
feasibility.documentary_complexity: Nominal 7 natural Sources. Operative terms, the named decision, payment instructions, cash postings, provider outcomes, period reconciliation and briefing each have a distinct business purpose. The inventory is an assumption for one cycle, not a practice estimate.
feasibility.infrastructure_reuse: Reuse C's joint proof and invariant-graph checks, B's origin tracing and existing independently rederived mask keys. Arithmetic is checked during proof review; no scorer extension is needed.
feasibility.ontology_compatibility: Score beneficiary_of and independent supported relationships only. Accounts, transactions, monetary limits, failure and payment instructions stay in evidence or the companion register.
risks_and_limits: The single intact file cannot identify a causal effect of seeing a failed transfer or of financial record load.
If the normal provider or trustee record resolves current status directly, the file may be defensible but the proposed cap-reconstruction mechanism is not isolated.

assumptions: The fictional operative terms identify the provision, define qualifying completed installments and state the exact consequence of exhausting the cap. Neither posting a debit nor instructing a reissue counts; no external payment-finality or trust law is needed.

The retained payment history covers every authorised installment from the start through the cut-off. The provider's linked return records affirmatively establish failure to complete, not a later clawback. The operative threshold has not previously been reached, so no revival rule is needed.

The trust accountant normally reconciles these cash movements but does not issue a legal roster. Provider records and accountant records have separate jobs; neither is excluded merely because it offers a shorter proof.
grounding.documentary_situation: A named provision ends only when distinct completed installments under that provision reach an express cumulative cap. One outward debit is returned because the transfer did not complete; the gross debits appear to reach the cap, but the documented completed installments do not. The file covers the full period of the provision through the review. It distinguishes a failed transfer from the recovery of an installment that had already completed.
grounding.legal_workflow: Reconcile the trust's elapsed payment cycle before advising on the next cycle under a capped provision.
grounding.meeting_purpose: Separate the current beneficiary relationship from the bank balance, the gross debit total and any proposed reissue.
practitioner_unknowns: Would a naturally administered finite provision expressly cease on completed installments, rather than only govern the amount payable under an otherwise continuing designation?
Would the provider's retained material distinguish debit posting from noncompletion and link the return to the exact attempt, and would the adviser ordinarily receive complete coverage at this stage?

references.relevance: Supports retaining payment records, expenses, distributions and the instruments relevant to administration. It does not establish the cap, qualifying-payment rule or meaning of a provider's status label.
references.title: HMRC · Records to keep for trusts

grounding.retainer: Advise whether a finite named provision remains operative at the first reconciliation after a failed installment attempt.

objective.coverage_gap: BG asks whether movement of assets between separate trusts propagates their relationships, not whether payments under one existing provision satisfy its quantitative cessation rule. AG tests complete negative receipt coverage, not classification and aggregation of several positive transactions with a failed attempt among them. AC switches an express expiry date and tests resumption; BO reconstructs a cumulative condition and requires no revival.
objective.failure_mechanism: An extractor may sum gross debits, count an installment twice because it appears in provider and ledger records, ignore the need for complete period coverage, or attach a payment entry instead of proof of the current provision.
objective.falsifiable_hypothesis: On the intact file, the cumulative amount of distinct qualifying completions remains below the express cap despite the apparent gross total. The named edge is recoverable with a sufficient same-edge subset that establishes that distinction. Correct complete recovery and attachment disconfirm the predicted errors on this file.

proposals.title: Posted debits do not necessarily exhaust a capped named benefit

stopping_criteria: At the documentary-realism gate, verify a distinct creator or business purpose, custody and ordinary availability at the cut-off for every proposed Source. Defer rather than pad the file, suppress a normally retained controlling record or invent a reporting convention solely to carry the proof.

Lock a proposal only after independent complete-file reconstruction, blind exact-excerpt review and bidirectional audit. Verify both the strongest support and the exact basis for exclusion or withholding. Credit any truly sufficient subset, check shorter alternatives and copies, and independently rederive each diagnostic key rather than assuming removal can only subtract edges.

For a matched pair, stop if the one literal edit changes another documentary fact, renders the fixed pack implausible or requires a second edit. For a natural-only file, never report review masks as scored siblings or evidence of a causal workload or placement effect.

Defer cases requiring outside law, unseen records, new node or predicate types, changes to the exact-name policy or chunked substitutes for independent whole-file reads. Keep human admission separate from technical qualification and preserve the admitted hypotheses, keys and scores.
